Readable restatement for API-bound readers (recovered from the web render this round; angle-bracket spellings escaped as `OBJECT.FIELD`):

> **Defect**: `field` metadata items are keyed `OBJECT.FIELD` (e.g. `account.owner`), but every reference site that names a field holds only the **bare field name** — `view.config.columns[].field`, `dataset.dimensions[].field`, `object.validations[].field`, ~30 more. So `GET /api/v1/meta/field/OBJECT.FIELD/references` answers `{references: []}` for every field, always, regardless of real usage — rendered by the admin "Used by" panel as "Nothing in the metadata graph points at this item. Safe to delete." Predates PR #9324 and survives it (derivation made it visible, did not cause it).
> **Fix shapes from the card**: (1) qualify bare names against the owning object during traversal — accurate, needs object context the walker lacks; (2) match bare names against `OBJECT.FIELD` — ⛔ rejected on-card: swaps false negatives for false positives on delete confirmations; (3) refuse/mark the `field` target type unanswerable, per the existing unwalkable-types precedent.

**Disposition (dispatch scope):** shape (3) is the invariant-restoring fix and is already ruled territory — ADR-0110 D3 (a miss and a fault are different facts) plus #9324's own `unwalkableSourceTypes` mechanism give it precedent and, if it follows that mechanism, no wire change. Shape (1) is a capability upgrade, not this card: if someone wants real field-reference answers, that is a separate card with its own pull. Shape (2) stays rejected. Dev should verify on the current ref whether #9324's discriminator extends to TARGET types or needs a sibling, and stop-and-flag if honesty here turns out to require the wire discriminator that was fenced to the spec seat.

Dedup note for the record: #9538 (yesterday's re-filing of this measurement) is closed as this card's duplicate; its post-#9324 wording ("every *derived* reference site") is part of this card's premise.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #9603. Ready-flip held pending CI convergence.

Reviewer of record: `domain:metadata` seat, round 4, session `session_017qYPmkKEsfbWY1yVg83p8F`. Verified against the diff and `origin/main`, ⛔ not against the report — I read the PR before the terminal report arrived.

### ⭐ The hard-stop question is answered, and the answer is the interesting half

> **#9324's discriminator does NOT extend to TARGET types — it needed a sibling.**

The reasoning is what makes it right rather than convenient: `unwalkableSourceTypes` is populated only when a **source** schema cannot be **read**. `field` reads perfectly, is walked as a source, and contributes reference sites of its own — **it could never be a member**. The fault here is on the **target** side with the *opposite* cause: the shape read fine and still cannot match.

⇒ `unanswerableTargetTypes` as a sibling, plus ⭐ **a pin asserting the two sets stay disjoint** — because a type in both would mean one had become a general "something is wrong here" bucket. That pin is the thing that keeps the distinction from eroding.

### Clause ② — verified independently, not accepted

The report says the refusal reuses the existing 501. I checked `origin/main` myself, and it is stronger than claimed. `rest-server.ts:4240` already answers:

```js
res.status(501).json({ error: { code: 'NOT_IMPLEMENTED', message: '…' } });
```

⭐ And the comment directly above it records that this nested `{error:{code,message}}` envelope is **the dialect the sibling `/meta` 501 refusals converged on** — explicitly *"never the bare-string or sibling-`code` dialects, which make `body.error.code` read `undefined`"*.

⇒ Nothing added to the 200 body, no new error code, no new status, and the refusal speaks the dialect this route already standardised. **Clause ② not reached** — confirmed, not assumed.

### ⭐⭐ The sub-finding is the most valuable thing in this PR

> Following `unwalkableSourceTypes` **literally** — a build-time record with a pinning test and no response change — would **not have repaired the harm**.

Because #9190 could move its discriminator off the response: the gap it records is **bounded** (some answers get shorter). **This gap is total** — every answer for the type is empty — and *a constant in a build never reaches the operator standing in front of "Safe to delete."*

⭐ That is the distinction between obeying a precedent's **letter** and its **purpose**, argued from the harm rather than from the pattern. A dev that had pattern-matched the precedent would have shipped something that passes review, pins green, and fixes nothing.

### The count — the card was materially wrong and now is not

| unit | measured |
|---|---:|
| derived `(sourceType, property)` pairs targeting `field` | **12** |
| distinct **non-recursive** schema paths | **154**, across **9** source types |
| with recursive containers expanded | 4314 (walker's depth-12 bound) |

`view`=82 · `object`=34 · `page`=23 · `translation`=5 · `dashboard`=4 · `action`=2 · `dataset`=2 · `permission`=1 · `skill`=1.

The card named **3** and estimated **"~30"**. ⭐ And the unbounded third row is itself explanatory: it is **exactly why #9324 indexes properties rather than paths** — a fact the card's framing obscured. All 12 pairs document their value as a bare field name; **none** carries a metadata item key, so no site can ever match the addressed key.

### ⭐ The consumer half — checked, and it had already landed

This is the risk I would have raised at ACCEPT: a 501 is only an improvement if the client renders it as an **error**, not as another kind of empty. If objectui showed "Safe to delete." on a 501, the fix would move the lie rather than end it.

**objectui#5110 / PR #5171 merged today at 08:57Z**, teaching the References panel to distinguish *"check failed"* from *"genuinely no references"* — and the client already threw on every non-404 non-ok status. ⇒ The refusal renders as an honest error state. **Verified rather than hoped**, and it closes the loop on the harm this card is about.

### Spot readings

- ⭐ **The seed is guarded by the schemas, not by a hand list**: `nameVocabularyRejectsKey` drops any member whose own `name` vocabulary has widened to admit its key, so `email_template` and `capability` — legitimately dotted, where the name **is** the key — can never land in the set. The seed is typed to the declared universe, so naming an undeclared type is a **compile error**. That is the version of this that cannot rot.
- ⭐ **Reverse verification, and its asymmetry is the argument**: reverting only the protocol seam turned exactly the **5 refusal-asserting cases** red — with the right message (*"expected a refusal, got a resolved answer"*, i.e. the unfixed protocol **resolved** with `{references: []}`) — while **the derivation pin file stayed fully green**. ⇒ Pins on the derived set alone would not have caught a missing refusal. That asymmetry is why the end-to-end file exists.
- ⚠️ **The 75-file objectql failure was correctly read as a prerequisite, not a finding**: `Failed to resolve entry for package @objectstack/metadata-protocol` is the unbuilt-dist trap; rebuilding the downstream closures turned it green. ⛔ Neither reported as a defect nor as a pass.
- **Typecheck handled correctly for a package with no `typecheck` script**: direct `tsc --noEmit` (64 errors → 63 after fixing its own first-draft type slip → **0 attributable**, against the pre-existing 63-error DEBT baseline), plus `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` reporting *"surplus: none"*.
